case_study_insert.main_stem: Brightwell Digital Media (BDM) is a partnership in the digital marketing and web-design sector, employing a workforce of 40. Founded in 2013 by Liam Okafor, the agency designs e-commerce websites and runs social media campaigns for small retail businesses and operates a flat structure with laissez-faire leadership. Brightwell plans to invest $450,000 in a new app-development studio, financed by a $250,000 bank loan and $200,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $175,000 a year, a variable cost of $8.00 a unit and a selling price of $15.00, and currently produces 45,000 units a year. The agency faces two problems: labour turnover is rising and client complaints about missed deadlines have increased.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Client Delivery Report — Q4 2025: The studio completed 3,200 billable project units last quarter with a rework rate of 4.1%, down from 6.0% a year earlier. Client complaints fell from 42 to 24 a month. Average project delivery time is 12 days. A survey of 300 small-business clients found that 61% would pay up to $0.40 more for faster turnaround, while 55% choose agencies on portfolio quality. A skills audit shows 12 of 40 staff need advanced coding training; external courses cost $950 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Brightwell Digital Media for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) The central bank lifted the base rate from 4.0% to 4.75%, raising variable-rate loan costs for small firms. (2) The minimum wage rises 6.2% from $12.80 to $13.59 an hour from April 2026. (3) Freelance developer day rates and software subscription input costs have risen 11.3% year-on-year, while digital advertising spend grew 5.6% and consumer price inflation is 3.9%.

questions.question_text: BDM plans to fund its $450,000 app-development studio with a $250,000 bank loan and $200,000 retained profit. Explain two advantages for BDM of using the $250,000 bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: The $250,000 bank loan lets Brightwell fund the full $450,000 app-development studio without draining the partnership's limited reserves, which matters for a 40-person agency with fixed costs of $175,000 a year. Retaining the $200,000 profit as working capital protects cash flow while the new studio is built and helps absorb the 11.3% rise in freelance developer day rates.

Point 2: Repaying the loan over time spreads the cost, so the agency does not have to wait until profits are large enough to self-fund. With a selling price of $15.00 and contribution of $7.00 a unit, the 45,000-unit output can service the loan gradually, letting Liam Okafor keep the partnership's own capital intact and pursue the studio immediately rather than delaying the launch. The agency's flat, 40-person structure and the 11.3% rise in freelance day rates make preserving the $200,000 reserve particularly sensible, because it gives Liam Okafor room to hire or subcontract when the new studio is at full capacity.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to the named business.

questions.question_text: BDM is promoting its new app-development studio. Consider local newspaper advertising, pay-per-click search advertising, or partnerships with business influencers. Which should BDM choose? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Local newspaper advertising: Print ads in local business papers would raise awareness among nearby small retailers and suit a 40-person agency, but readership is ageing and narrow, response is slow, and the $450,000 studio needs a wider pipeline than one locality can supply. Costs are fixed regardless of results, so waste is high.

Pay-per-click search advertising: Buying keywords such as 'e-commerce website design' puts Brightwell in front of retailers actively searching for its service, with tight budgets and measurable clicks, which suits a firm with fixed costs of $175,000. The drawback is that competitive keywords are expensive, clicks do not guarantee contracts, and the 11.3% rise in freelance developer rates means each lost bid still consumes scarce staff time.

Partnerships with business influencers: Collaborating with respected small-business commentators builds trust and demonstrates portfolio quality, which the survey shows matters to 55% of 300 clients; it also reaches a national audience at manageable cost. Results take time to build and depend on the influencer's credibility, but content can be reused. Budget control is decisive here: with fixed costs of $175,000 and a $250,000 loan to service, pay-per-click spend can be capped daily, whereas newspaper space and event fees must be committed upfront regardless of the enquiries they generate.

Recommendation: BDM should choose pay-per-click search advertising as the primary channel, supported by influencer content. It delivers measurable, high-intent enquiries quickly and can be capped to protect cash, directly filling the pipeline for the $250,000-loan-funded studio. Local newspaper advertising is rejected as narrow and unmeasurable, and influencer partnerships alone are rejected as too slow to generate the immediate project volume needed to justify a $450,000 investment.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited outline of promotional options with minimal application to BDM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discussion of advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in BDM's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three options in BDM's context with a justified recommendation explaining why newspaper advertising and influencer partnerships are rejected.

questions.question_text: BDM's labour turnover is rising. Explain two benefits for BDM of using job enrichment to motivate its web designers and reduce turnover.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Job enrichment gives BDM's designers more varied, challenging work — for example owning a project from brief to launch — which satisfies esteem and self-actualisation needs (Maslow) and makes the 40-strong team feel valued. Higher job satisfaction should reduce the rising labour turnover and protect the 3,200 billable units delivered last quarter.

Point 2: Enriched roles give designers greater responsibility and recognition for portfolio quality, which the survey shows 55% of clients use when choosing an agency. More engaged staff are likely to cut the 4.1% rework rate and the 42 monthly complaints, reducing the pressure on Liam Okafor's flat laissez-faire structure and avoiding repeated $950-per-employee replacement training costs. These benefits are realistic for a 40-person partnership with a flat laissez-faire structure, where designers already expect autonomy; enrichment formalises that freedom around clear project ownership. It also complements the $0.40 faster-turnaround premium that 61% of the 300 surveyed clients accept, giving staff a tangible link between their enriched work and higher revenue.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to the named business.

questions.question_text: BDM needs experienced app developers for its new studio. Consider internal recruitment or external recruitment. Which should BDM choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
Internal recruitment: Promoting existing staff is cheap, fast and motivational, and the candidates already understand Brightwell's systems and the 40-person culture, so they can contribute to the $450,000 studio immediately. It avoids agency fees and the risk of a bad hire. However, the skills audit shows 12 of 40 staff need advanced coding training and the firm already faces rising labour turnover, so the internal pool may lack the specialist app skills required and promotion leaves gaps elsewhere.

External recruitment: Hiring experienced app developers from outside brings proven skills and fresh ideas, filling the gap the skills audit identified without a long training lead-in. This supports the 3,200-unit delivery record and the 4.1% rework target. The costs are higher — advertising, interviews and possible agency fees — and new starters need induction, while a 40-person partnership with fixed costs of $175,000 must be careful about adding pay bill. Cost must be weighed against speed: the $450,000 studio needs developers who can work on app projects from day one, and the 12 of 40 staff needing advanced coding training cannot be trained quickly enough to fill that gap. External hiring also spreads the risk of the 4.1% rework target being missed through inexperience.

Decision: BDM should choose external recruitment for the senior app-developer roles, with internal candidates developed through the $950 courses for future positions. External hiring is justified because the studio needs skills the audit shows are missing and the $250,000 loan gives the funds; internal recruitment is rejected as unable to supply the required expertise quickly and as likely to disrupt existing delivery while turnover is already rising.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two recruitment methods with limited application to BDM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of one or both methods in BDM's context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods in BDM's context with a well-justified decision covering skills, cost and disruption.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how BDM's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Margin of safety = Actual output − Break-even output. Substitution: Break-even = $175,000 ÷ ($15.00 − $8.00) = $175,000 ÷ $7.00 = 25,000 units; margin of safety = 45,000 − 25,000 = 20,000 units. Answer: margin of safety is 20,000 units.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $15.00 − $8.00 = $7.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $7.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways BDM's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. A margin of safety of 20,000 units above the 25,000 break-even point shows the agency can withstand a demand fall before losing money, guiding how aggressively to use the $250,000 loan.
2. Contribution per unit of $7.00 lets managers test the survey finding that 61% of 300 clients would pay $0.40 more for faster turnaround; a $0.40 premium lifts contribution to $7.40.
3. Fixed costs of $175,000 and $7.00 contribution set the volume needed to service the $450,000 studio loan, so managers can judge whether 45,000 units is sufficient.
4. Average total cost of $11.89 ($175,000 ÷ 45,000 + $8.00) enables benchmarking against the 4.1% rework rate and helps decide whether to accept more work at the $15.00 price as developer rates rise 11.3%.

questions.model_answer: (i) Margin of safety = 20,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $7.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety vs 25,000 break-even; $0.40 premium modelling from the 300-client survey; loan servicing for the $450,000 studio; unit-cost benchmarking at $11.89.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method and 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii); 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate BDM's financial position by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and return on capital employed for 2024 and 2025. Which ratio gives the strongest evidence of improvement? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 36.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 42.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 10.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 14.0%
ROCE 2024 = 15.0%
ROCE 2025 = 20.0%

Detailed workings (all figures $'000): 2024 gross margin = 324 ÷ 900 × 100 = 36.0%; 2025 = 420 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 42.0%. Operating return on sales 2024 = 90 ÷ 900 × 100 = 10.0%; 2025 = 140 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 14.0%. Return on capital 2024 = 90 ÷ 600 × 100 = 15.0%; 2025 = 140 ÷ 700 × 100 = 20.0%. Cost of sales was almost flat, rising from 576 to 580, while revenue grew from 900 to 1,000.

Evaluation: All three measures improved, so BDM's financial position has strengthened. The gross margin rising from 36.0% to 42.0% reflects tight control of direct project costs despite the 11.3% rise in freelance developer rates, and the operating return on sales improving from 10.0% to 14.0% shows the flat 40-person structure is absorbing overheads better. Return on capital improved from 15.0% to 20.0%, meaning the 600 to 700 of capital employed is working harder, which supports the $450,000 studio. The strongest evidence is the 20.0% return on capital, because it shows the partnership is earning markedly more from the funds invested, not just recording higher sales. A caveat is that interest payable rose from 12 to 15 as the $250,000 loan is serviced.

Conclusion: BDM's financial position has improved on all three measures. The rise in return on capital from 15.0% to 20.0% is the clearest signal of value creation; the growing interest bill is the main residual risk to watch.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the three ratios for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years, detailed evaluation of cost, revenue and capital movements, and a justified conclusion naming the strongest evidence.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for BDM of introducing automated code-testing software to reduce its 4.1% rework rate.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Automated testing would catch defects before delivery, directly reducing the 4.1% rework rate and the 42 monthly client complaints recorded in the Client Delivery Report. Fewer errors lower the $8.00 variable cost per unit of fixing code, protect the $15.00 selling price and support the 3,200 billable-unit record, helping the 40-person agency justify its $450,000 studio investment.

Disadvantage: Testing software adds a licence cost on top of fixed costs of $175,000 at a time when the $250,000 loan must be serviced and developer day rates have risen 11.3%. In a flat laissez-faire structure with a skills gap (12 of 40 staff need training), staff may resist or misuse the tool, and automated checks cannot replace the client judgement that 55% of survey respondents value in portfolio quality. BDM should pilot the tool on one project team before rollout, checking whether the 12-day delivery average and 55% portfolio-quality criterion improve, so that the $450,000 studio is not burdened with an ineffective system.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid point identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to the named business.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the base rate rise to 4.75%, the 6.2% minimum wage increase and the 11.3% rise in freelance developer input costs will affect BDM. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.0% to 4.75%): If BDM's $250,000 loan is variable-rate, the extra 0.75% costs 0.75% × $250,000 = $1,875 a year — modest against fixed costs of $175,000 and interest payable of 15 ($'000). If the loan is fixed, the effect is nil. Higher rates could raise the cost of any further borrowing for the $450,000 studio, but the partnership can limit this by fixing the rate.

Minimum wage increase (6.2%, to $13.59 an hour): The insert gives no hours worked or individual pay, so an annual wage total cannot be invented. The sound judgement is qualitative: with a workforce of 40, a compulsory rise lifts costs that cannot be avoided and squeezes the $7.00 contribution per unit unless productivity holds or the $15.00 price rises; the survey's 61% willing to pay $0.40 more for speed offers one route to recovery.

Freelance developer input costs (11.3%): BDM relies on outside developers, and the insert does not split the $8.00 variable cost, so only a bound is defensible: if the whole $8.00 rose 11.3%, that is 11.3% × $8.00 = $0.90 per unit, and at 45,000 units about $40,700 a year. Even a $0.40 rise would cost $18,000 a year, cutting contribution toward $6.60 and threatening the 3,200-unit delivery plan.

Conclusion: The 11.3% rise in freelance developer input costs will have the greatest impact because it hits every one of the 45,000 units and directly erodes the contribution that supports the $450,000 studio. The wage rise is real but not quantifiable from the insert, and the roughly $1,875 interest effect is small; BDM should favour in-house hiring and the $0.40 premium.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external factors with limited application to BDM.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on BDM's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in BDM's context with a well-justified greatest-impact judgement and reasons why the other two are smaller.
